mesh: Read the existing Gmsh .msh file specified by the card as a finite element mesh.
Access the imported mesh data: the mesh, its cell and boundary markers, and the physical-group information.
Associate the card's tagged regions with the marker tables of the corresponding entity dimensions.
Define volume and exterior-boundary integration measures on the imported mesh, associating each measure with the corresponding marker table so that tagged regions can be selected for integration.
function_space: Prepare UFL-compatible finite elements for the fields and combine their components into a mixed element where required, following the card's families, degrees and value shapes.
Create the function spaces on the existing mesh and initialize persistent finite element coefficient fields for the unknowns and internal states.
Prepare the trial and test arguments on each selected function space in the declared field order, using component arguments for a mixed variational form.
weak_form: Define coefficients that are constant with respect to the domain for the supplied material parameters, loads, and sources.
Reconfigure the prepared integration measures with the card's selected subdomains and metadata to construct the supplied weak forms from their kinematic and constitutive expressions.
boundary_conditions: Get all entity indices with a given mesh-tag value from the marker tables prepared by the mesh stage.

Retrieve the i-th subspace of the original finite element space for a constrained component and, when required, convert it into a new standalone function space with a map from new to old degrees of freedom; use the parent space for whole-field constraints.
Locate degrees of freedom belonging to the boundary mesh entities topologically, then create Dirichlet boundary conditions using those degrees of freedom and the prescribed values.
solve: For a linear formulation, construct a high-level linear variational problem using PETSc from the prepared forms and boundary conditions.
For a nonlinear formulation, construct a high-level nonlinear variational problem using PETSc from the prepared residual, derivatives, and boundary conditions.
Apply the card's solver settings, solve the variational problem to update its stored fields, and check convergence before committing any required states.
